english: For $k>0$, let $f_{k}:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ be defined by $f_{k}(x)=\dfrac{x^{3}+3kx}{4k}$. If the area of the region bounded by the graphs of $f_{k}$ and its inverse function $f_{k}^{-1}$ is $50$, then the value of $k$ is ______.
hindi: $k>0$ के लिए, माना कि $f_{k}:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, $f_{k}(x)=\dfrac{x^{3}+3kx}{4k}$ द्वारा परिभाषित है। यदि $f_{k}$ तथा उसके प्रतिलोम फलन $f_{k}^{-1}$ के आलेखों द्वारा परिबद्ध क्षेत्र का क्षेत्रफल $50$ है, तो $k$ का मान ______ है।
solution: $f_{k}'(x)=\dfrac{3x^{2}+3k}{4k}>0$, so $f_{k}$ is a strictly increasing bijection; its graph and that of $f_{k}^{-1}$ meet only on $y=x$ and are mirror images in $y=x$.
solution_full: $f_{k}'(x)=\dfrac{3(x^{2}+k)}{4k}>0$ for all $x$, and $f_{k}(x)\to\pm\infty$ as $x\to\pm\infty$, so $f_{k}$ is a strictly increasing bijection of $\mathbb{R}$ and $f_{k}^{-1}$ exists.

For an increasing function, $f_{k}(x)=f_{k}^{-1}(x)$ implies $f_{k}(f_{k}(x))=x$, which forces $f_{k}(x)=x$ (if $f_{k}(x)>x$ then $f_{k}(f_{k}(x))>f_{k}(x)>x$, and similarly for $<$). So the two graphs meet only on $y=x$, at $f_{k}(x)=x$: $x^{3}+3kx=4kx\Rightarrow x(x^{2}-k)=0\Rightarrow x=0,\pm\sqrt{k}$.
The graph of $f_{k}^{-1}$ is the mirror image of that of $f_{k}$ in $y=x$, so the area between $f_{k}$ and $f_{k}^{-1}$ is twice the area between $f_{k}$ and $y=x$.
$x-f_{k}(x)=\dfrac{4kx-x^{3}-3kx}{4k}=\dfrac{x(k-x^{2})}{4k}$, positive on $(0,\sqrt k)$. Since $f_{k}$ is odd, the piece over $(-\sqrt k,0)$ has the same area.
originality_note: New: a one-parameter family of odd increasing cubics whose fixed points are 0 and +-sqrt k, so that the area with the inverse is linear in k (way 5). Closest known: area between y = x^2/(4a) type curve and its inverse (two parabolas). Different because: the inverse has no usable closed form, the region has two pieces (first and third quadrants), and the reflection argument is essential.

concept_use.Area bounded by a curve and its inverse: The graphs of f_k and f_k^-1 are mirror images in y = x and meet only there, so the area is twice the area between f_k and y = x, giving k/4.

stem_review: Read as a student: every function and curve introduced with its domain, every condition stated, one reading, answer unique and equal to the plan; Hindi mirrors the English maths. Checked bijectivity (f' > 0) so the inverse exists, and that the graphs meet only on y = x. No change.
key_step: Reduce to twice the area between f_k and y = x.
justification: Standard reflection argument plus a routine integral and two-piece symmetry; L2 like 2024-P2-Q2.
blueprint_concepts: Area bounded by a curve and its inverse
